data.narrative:
QuamCore is a Series A quantum computing company founded by Alon Cohen that has raised $35M to date. The sector comprises 11 total comparables—3 public (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion—though the narrow peer set at identical stage and valuation tier remains constrained.

The valuation analysis relies on a single applicable triangulation method: stage-progression. Using the $35M total raised as a proxy for current implied valuation, application of a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-subsequent-stage progression yields $70M. The peer-median method is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage datapoints within the quantum computing sector; a forced reliance on all-sector medians would lack sufficient specificity to inform the valuation meaningfully.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $60M to $80M, with a median point of $70M. This single-method output carries material uncertainty around the stage-progression multiplier itself—the 2.0x assumption may not reflect QuamCore's specific capital efficiency, product maturity, or market conditions relative to the broader quantum computing cohort. Additional data on revenue run-rate, customer traction, or technology differentiation would strengthen conviction in this range.
